title: Prefix evaluation ordering bug causing misattributed metering on composite routes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: We are seeing cases where requests routed to composite route aliases are metered against the wrong evaluation bucket when the route prefix list contains overlapping keys (e.g., /v1/chat and /v1/chat/enterprise). This causes undercounting for higher-privilege routes and overcounting for the base route. Impacted components: prefix matcher in the policy-evaluator, route alias resolution, shard-aggregator.

Observed behavior: During a traffic spike on enterprise customers using a long route prefix, telemetry shows an anomalous drop in credits consumed for the enterprise route and a corresponding unexplained increase on the base route. Affected customers reported quota overruns not being enforced for ~10–30s windows during the spike.

Why this is unique: Unlike prior "shadowing" issues, this is triggered by ordering and race between prefix cache refresh and the new policy hot-reload path when overlapping prefixes exist. The runtime incorrectly binds an incoming token to the first matching prefix it finds in the in-memory list rather than the longest-prefix match semantics that our policy language guarantees.

Repro steps (deterministic in staging):
1) Load policy set with overlapping prefixes: /v1/chat (base) and /v1/chat/enterprise (enterprise).
2) Start steady background traffic to /v1/chat at 80% of base quota.
3) Begin a short (30s) burst from a single enterprise test org to /v1/chat/enterprise at 200% of enterprise quota.
4) Trigger a policy hot-reload (simulated using test control plane) during the burst.
5) Observe that ~20–40% of enterprise requests are counted against /v1/chat for 10–40s in aggregator metrics (see dashboards).

Telemetry and evidence:
- Dashboard: https://grafana.internal.redwood/r/dashboard/boardX?panel=prefix-mismatch-spike (internal)
- Sample logs: /var/logs/policy-evaluator/2026-03-10-prefix-incident.log (attached to the ticket via Drive link)
- Repro trace: trace ID trace-20260310-enterprise-42 (shows match decision and cache_version at evaluation)

Initial hypothesis: A combination of non-deterministic iteration order over the prefix set after hot-reload + an optimization in the fast-path matcher that returns on first match (instead of longest match) is to blame. The hot-reload path replaces the prefix vector atomically but does not guarantee sorted order; earlier versions relied on a sorted invariant that is no longer enforced when policies are compiled in parallel.

Root cause (found after instrumented run):
- Policy compiler produces a slice of prefix entries without stable sorting when multiple compile workers operate concurrently.
- The fast-path matcher uses an O(n) scan and returns the first match to minimize checks, assuming the slice is pre-sorted by prefix length. After hot-reload the iteration order can have the longer prefix appear after the shorter prefix, causing a premature match.
- The metering layer attaches the resolved route id at match time; subsequent aggregation keys are therefore wrong for the remainder of the request and for KV caching of prefetch credits.

Immediate mitigation (done):
- Rollback: Reverted the recent change to parallel policy compilation in the staging control plane on 2026-03-10 22:15 UTC — this eliminated the repro in staging.
- Hotfix: Added a guard in the runtime matcher to perform a secondary length-check when an overlapping prefix pattern is detected. Deployed to staging (PR #5821). This reduces exposure but is a stopgap (still O(n) in worst case).

Long-term fix (planned):
1) Ensure the policy compiler emits prefix tables sorted by descending length and with deterministic stable ordering (compiler change in runtime-compiler module).
2) Replace first-match fast-path with a trie-based longest-prefix match structure for O(k) matching, where k is prefix length. This will also standardize binding semantics and be more efficient at scale.
3) Add unit+integration tests that exercise overlapping-prefix hot-reload scenarios and assert stable attribution across concurrent compiles.

Acceptance criteria for closure: 
- Deterministic repro cannot be triggered in staging after fix; aggregator counts align within 0.1% expected for both routes during repro bursts.
- Canary rollout to 10% of runtime nodes for 48 hours with canary metrics showing no misattribution.
- Backfill detection job to re-evaluate suspect windows for customer-facing support (see follow-ups).

Implementation plan & timeline:
- 2026-03-11: Compiler patch (ENG-763210-compilersort branch) — in review (PR #5899). (owner: Marco Ruiz)
- 2026-03-13: Trie matcher implementation started (owner: David Chen). Estimated 3 dev days.
- 2026-03-16: End-to-end tests + canary rollout.
- 2026-03-18: Production rollout if canary stable.

Work items / TODOs:
- [ ] Finish compiler deterministic sort impl (PR feedback from research).
- [ ] Finish trie-based matcher and replace fast-path.
- [ ] Add regression test harness that runs hot-reload + burst patterns in CI.
- [ ] Run backfill detection for last 7 days to identify impacted orgs and produce support tickets.
- [ ] Postmortem doc and customer communications draft.

Links to artifacts and references:
- Draft postmortem (Confluence): https://confluence.internal.redwood/pages/PM-ENG/prefix-hotreload-postmortem
- Staging PR (hotfix): https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/5821
- Compiler PR (in review): https://github.com/redwood/runtime-compiler/pull/5899
- Trie matcher WIP branch: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/tree/eng-763210-trie-matcher

Notes from code review and design discussion:
- "We should prefer a deterministic canonicalization step as close to compile output as possible; relying on matchers to correct ordering is brittle." — Linnea Svensson (reviewer)
- "Trie will give us consistent semantics and better perf for deep prefix sets; implement memory-efficient nodes and share common prefixes." — Priya Kapoor (architecture)
